title: 2  Masters Topics
text:
2.1 Simulation of a Synchronous Reluctance Machine
A synchronous reluctance motor is a type of electric motor which operates on the principles of magnetic reluctance.
Unlike traditional motors, which rely on electromagnets or permanent magnets, synchronous reluctance motors generate torque through the rotor’s reluctance to the magnetic field which is generated by the stator.
This results in a highly efficient motor with a simpler construction.
Additional information on these kinds of motor can be found here.

title: 2  Masters Topics
text:
2.2 Analog Computer for Solving ODEs
Analog computer are a class of devices whereby continuously variable physical quantities, (i.e., electrical potential) are represented in a way that is analogous to the corresponding quantities in the problem to be solved. The analog system is set up according to initial conditions and then allowed to change freely.
Answers to the problem are obtained by measuring the variables in the analog model and are seeing a resurgence as a good alternative to digital computers.
There are numerous examples such as the Phillip’s Machine which was used to determine the economic process at a national level using fluidic logic, or the Robert’s Machine which was used to determine the tides. An interesting article by Quanta magazine on Analog computers is also worth a quick read.
The work of this thesis is to design, test, and construct an electrical circuit which is capable of solving 1st- and 2nd-order Ordinary Differential Equations given to the circuit as input.
As an example, using the circuit, the behavior of a mass-damper-spring system will be simulated:
\[m \frac{d^2x}{dt^2} + c\frac{dx}{dt} + kx = f(x),\]
where the values of the mass (\(m\)), damper (\(c\)) and spring (\(k\)) will be set using a signal generator. To design this computer, the student will have to work on;

The Design of the circuit logic which allows configurable options to solve a wide variety of equations,
Implementation of analog circuits and designing appropriate filters to minimize circuit noise.


2.2.1 Test
To achieve the aforementioned effectively, the following are required:

Working understanding with Printed Circuit Boards,
Circuit design and soldering.
Understanding Ordinary Differential Equations are a plus.

title: 2  Masters Topics
text:
2.3 Fault Detection in Electrical Machines
Electrical machines, while the backbone of residential, commercial and industrial settings, are nevertheless, prone to numerous faults and require constant monitoring to ensure safe and dependable functioning.
A potential fault in electrical machinery results in unscheduled downtime, necessitating the prompt assessment of any abnormal circumstances in rotating electrical machines.
The work will require to implement machine learning algorithms for the service of fault detection. To achieve the required application, the student is required to have a working knowledge of:

A good understanding of machine learning/signal processing is preferred,
A strong background in programming,
Working knowledge of electrodynamics is beneficial.

The outcome will be a work producing a possible novel approach to detecting electrical faults in an electrical motor.
The student will gain significant experience working with signal processing and programming and developing large machine learning algorithms.

title: 2  Masters Topics
section: 2.4 Vector Control of Induction Motors using Embedded Computing
text:
2.4 Vector Control of Induction Motors using Embedded Computing
While AC motors have shown to be reliable and performing well, it was not the case 30+ years ago. Then, majority of machines used in industry would have been based on DC machines. The primary reason for their abundance was due to their simplicity in control. Then, with the advent of vector control AC machines were able to catch up in terms of efficiency and control.
This thesis will focus on designing the vector control for the use of primarily induction machines which the student will have access to. The coding and the logic of the vector control will be implemented on an embedded computing, which will the ESP32.
To achieve this construction the student should have a working knowledge of:

A solid understanding of the principles of vector control and induction machine modeling.
Knowledge of designing an inverter,
Previous experience on working with Embedded Systems or good knowledge in C.

The outcome will be a fully functional test-bed with an induction motor controlled using vector control method.

title: 3  Bachelors Thesis
section: 3.2 Design and Implementation of Cyclic Redundancy Check for Transmission
text:
3.2 Design and Implementation of Cyclic Redundancy Check for Transmission
A cyclic redundancy check is an error-detecting code used in digital communication networks and storage systems to detect accidental changes to raw data. Blocks of data that are transmitted get a short check value attached to the block code, based on the remainder of a polynomial division of their contents. When retrieved, the calculation is redone and, in the event the check values do not match (i.e., when an error occurs during transmission), an action can be taken against data corruption.
This project will involve an experimental design of a communication system involving two Arduinos. These two Arduinos will communicate with each other and check each transmitted message using CRCs. The user will introduce errors externally (i.e., drawing a magnet next to wires, or creating cross-talk) and observe the output from a display attached to the Arduinos.
To achieve this test bed, the students is required to have:

A good experience in programming C/C++,
Designing of logic circuits,
A good understanding of communication network topics.

The outcome will be a fully functional experimental test-bed which will be used as a showcase of communication concepts.

section: 3.3 Design of a DC Motor Test Bench
text:
3.3 Design of a DC Motor Test Bench
The students should have knowledge of:

Circuit design,
CAD software experience,
Basic knowledge on electric machines is a plus.

DC Drives are one of the more versatile machines still used in industry due to their cost effective design and simple control methodologies. One of the advantages is their ability to adapt based on how their wiring is done for field and armature. This work will require the construction of a DC motor test bench for use in electric machine lectures.
The outcome will be a working platform where the machine dynamic can be changed based on how the connections are done. These connections will be designed in a way as to easily be changed by the user. The student shall also gain practical experience with electric drive design and work with manufacturing of a product which takes different parts of electrical engineering and combine them. The student will also contribute to the development of new hardware to be used by the next generation of students.

title: 3  Bachelors Thesis
section: 3.4 Simulation of GNSS within the Gazebo Environment
text:
3.4 Simulation of GNSS within the Gazebo Environment
The problem he tackled was the fact that GNSS receivers have only very basic support in simulators for mobile robotics. The currently available simulated sensors have a very unfaithful error model of the estimated positions (usually only additive Gaussian noise or a small random walk). If you’ve ever worked with a real GNSS receiver, you know that this is far from what you get in reality.
One of the most important factors that influence the computed position and its covariance is the visibility of the satellites. It influences both the DOP (dilution of precision), i.e., the geometry of the visible parts of constellations, and the convergence of the position estimation algorithm.
Václav has implemented a raytracing algorithm that detects which satellites are hidden behind scene objects (buildings, vegetation, etc.) and computes a full-fledged RINEX observation log with only the unblocked signals or with some signals damaged (if they, e.g., passed through a tree). The algorithm can even simulate cycle slips for phase measurements if some satellite disappeared for a while and then was found again. You can use your favorite RINEX processing tool to get the position and covariance estimates.
Our future direction is making the simulation model more complete (including atmospheric effects), also implementing the position estimation part in Gazebo/ROS using the standard interfaces, and making the plugin actually usable by the community (as the current version is not yet production quality software).

title: 4  Thesis Guidelines
text:
4.1.1 Weekly Reports
It is a good idea that I receive weekly reports written in English from you.

It keeps you on track towards your advanced degree by making you read and think more.
It allows me to measure your progress in a qualitative way.

I will make comments on your repots (grammar, logic, contents, etc.). By the time you start to write your great papers/theses (and many of your works will be great) your command of English will be such that writing in it no longer terrifies you. I also got to enjoy benefit of amortizing the time of revising your later works (hopefully).
A weekly report is expected from
All Ph.D. students. 2nd-year-to-be-and-up Master’s students. Other current students of mine who care to write me a report.
A weekly report can be one of the following:

Your thesis draft.
A summary of the academic paper(s) you are reading. Now, if you read only 1-2 pages, summarize those 1-2 pages.
A summary of anything that you read (CNN reports, Time magazine articles, a novel, anything).
Opinion on anything (current events, arts, movies, music, politics, etc.).
Please note:
Your report should be one paragraph long and not exceed 1 page (unless it is your thesis draft). At the bottom of the report, list the academic papers you plan to read (unless you are a Ph.D. student who is already writing a thesis). That will give me a good idea where your research is heading. Sequence the file name of your report by yourstudentID-reportno. For example, if your student ID is r92922099 and this is your 5th report, make it r92922099005.doc. Download your template from http://www.csie.ntu.edu.tw/~lyuu/r99922099_001.doc Use Microsoft Word unless you are sending me a paper draft, in which case it can be either in PDF or LaTeX format. Email your report with your NTU (preferred) or NTUCSIE email account which uses the student ID as the user name. That will save me time identifying you and replying to you. You may want to read my Better Dissertation Writing in English for some helpful tips.

• Project Progress: o Briefly summarize the progress made on your research project during the past week. o Highlight any significant achievements, milestones, or challenges encountered. • Literature Review: o Provide an overview of the relevant literature you have reviewed or studied. o Summarize key findings, methodologies, and concepts related to your research. • Methodology and Experimentation: o Describe the methodologies, techniques, or experiments you have employed or conducted. o Include details such as materials, procedures, data collection methods, and any modifications made. • Results and Analysis: o Present and discuss the results obtained from your experiments or data analysis. o Include any tables, graphs, or figures to support your findings. Provide a critical analysis/interpretation of the results. • Challenges and Solutions: o Identify any challenges or obstacles you encountered during your research. o Discuss the strategies or solutions you implemented to overcome these challenges. • Future Work: o Outline your planned next steps and objectives for the upcoming week. o Specify any additional experiments, analyses, or literature review tasks you intend to undertake. • Questions and Discussion Points: o List any questions or concerns you have for further discussion during the group meeting. o Include any topics you would like to discuss with your supervisor or fellow researchers. • Personal Development and Learning: o Reflect on any new skills, knowledge, or insights gained during the week. o Discuss any seminars, workshops, or training sessions attended. • Other Updates: o Mention any relevant updates, announcements, or collaborations with other researchers or teams.
This template is a guideline, and you are encouraged to adapt it to suit the specific requirements and goals of your research project.
A basic template is given in here.






ImportantThesis GitHub Repo



It is mandatory for all students to create a repo on Github for their weekly reports. You will add your weekly report to this project (each section could have the title “Week starting DD/MM/YY”). Also, please email your supervisor a PDF copy of the report before the group meeting. Please check the USEFUL LINKS on the Lab Website to learn more about naming the project on Overleaf and some suggestions for the weekly report.








ImportantKeeping On Track



We will keep organizing the weekly meeting in a hybrid mode, but we strongly encourage everyone to attend the in-person group meeting. If you cannot attend the group meeting, kindly notify your supervisor via email and briefly explain the reason for your absence.
